routes.label: Remove trailing zeros and track remainders

question: The number obtained from the last two nonzero digits of \(90!\) is equal to \(n.\) What is \(n?\)
solution:
Each trailing zero comes from a factor of \(10=2\cdot5\). Among the factors of \(90!\), the 18 multiples of 5 each supply one factor of 5, and the three multiples of 25 supply one additional factor each. Thus there are exactly \(18+3=21\) factors of 5. There are at least 45 factors of 2, one from each even number, so \(90!\) has exactly 21 trailing zeros. Let
\[
M=\frac{90!}{10^{21}}.
\]
We will determine the final two digits of \(M\) by finding its remainders modulo 25 and modulo 4.

Let \(P(r)\) be the product of the positive integers at most \(r\) that are not divisible by 5. Separating the multiples of 5 twice gives
\[
90!=5^{18}P(90)\,18!
     =5^{21}P(90)P(18)\,3!.
\]
Therefore
\[
2^{21}M=P(90)P(18)\cdot6.
\]

The four numbers not divisible by 5 in any block of five have a convenient product modulo 25. Indeed,
\[
\begin{aligned}
(5j+1)(5j+4)&=25j(j+1)+4,\\
(5j+2)(5j+3)&=25j(j+1)+6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their product is consequently congruent to \(4\cdot6=24\equiv-1\pmod{25}\). There are 18 complete blocks in \(P(90)\), whereas \(P(18)\) has three complete blocks followed by \(16,17,18\). Hence
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(90)&\equiv(-1)^{18}=1\pmod{25},\\
P(18)&\equiv(-1)^3\cdot16\cdot17\cdot18
\equiv4\pmod{25}.
\end{aligned}
\]
It follows that \(2^{21}M\equiv24\pmod{25}\). Since \(2^{10}=1024\equiv-1\pmod{25}\), we have \(2^{21}\equiv2\pmod{25}\). Thus \(2M\equiv24\pmod{25}\), and cancellation of 2 is valid because 2 and 25 have no common factor. Therefore \(M\equiv12\pmod{25}\).

Removing the 21 factors of 2 still leaves at least \(45-21=24\), so \(M\) is divisible by 4. Its possible remainders modulo 100 are \(12,37,62,87\), and only 12 is divisible by 4. Thus \(M\) ends in 12. The requested number is \(\boxed{12}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
